chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abdullah ibn Uthman, from Abu Isma'il al-Sarraj, from Abdullah ibn Waddah and Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Isma'il ibn al-Arqat and his mother Umm Salama, sister of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I was ill in the month of Ramadan with a severe illness until I was near death. The Banu Hashim gathered at night for the funeral, thinking I was dead. My mother grieved over me, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to her, 'My sister, go up to the upper room, look toward the sky, and pray two rak'ahs. When you have finished the greeting (salam), say: O God, You gave me a gift which was nothing; O God, I have asked You for it anew, so lend it to me.' She did so, and I regained consciousness, sat up, and they brought suhoor for them, a porridge, which they ate for suhoor, and I ate with them.

And with this chain of narration, from Abu Isma'il al-Sarraj, from Ibn Muskhan, from Shurhabil al-Kindi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: 'When you wish to ask your Lord for something, perform ablution and do it well, then pray two rak'ahs, magnify Allah (the Mighty and Majestic), and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). After the greeting, say: O God, I ask You because You are a Generous King, and You are capable of all things, and You do whatever You will. O God, I turn to You through Your Prophet Muhammad, the Prophet of Mercy, peace be upon him and his family. O Muhammad, O Messenger of God, I turn to God through you, to my Lord and your Lord, that You may grant my request through you. O God, through Your Prophet, grant my request through Muhammad.' Then ask for your need.

key_terms.أَتَوَجَّهُ: I turn/face (towards God through an intermediary)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific prayer and supplication for recovering from illness or fulfilling a need according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter of Salat al-Mudtir (Prayer of the Needy) illustrates the efficacy of intercession (tawassul) through the Ahl al-Bayt, as Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) recounts his miraculous recovery via his aunt's prayer. It establishes a specific ritual format for seeking divine aid, emphasizing the Prophet Muhammad as the means of approach to Allah, a concept deeply rooted in Shia theological tradition regarding the spiritual authority of the Imams.
